relationships.evidence_quote: We found that CGRP increased firing in both the right and left CeA neurons.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: we found that CGRP administration in the right CeA increased behavioral signs of bladder pain and decreased bladder pain-like behavior when administered in the left CeA.

relationships.subject: CGRP(8-37)
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP(8–37), however, blocked the effects of optogenetic stimulation on bladder pain-like physiology (Fig. 4B–C), suggesting that CGRP release is responsible for optogenetic-induced lateralized changes in bladder pain.

relationships.subject: parabrachial nucleus
relationships.evidence_quote: Using CGRP-knockout animals, we established that it is indeed the action of CGRP released from the PBN that drives right CeA-optogenetically-mediated hyperalgesia and left CeA-optogenetically-mediated anti-hyperalgesia in bladder pain.

key_findings: CGRP from PBN to CeA terminals drives opposing lateralized modulation of bladder pain: pro-nociceptive in right CeA, anti-nociceptive in left CeA
CGRP increases CeA neuron firing in both hemispheres; Calcrl expression does not differ by side, but CGRP expression falls in left CeA after cyclophosphamide
